mainTopic: Partial or incomplete offerings outside the עזרה: קטורת and wine, lacking items, חציצה, a mixed קומץ, and the קומץ and לבונה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about burning part of the קטורת outside: does putting an amount in a vessel make it one fixed unit? Following the view that the vessel does not matter, רבא shows that pouring wine outside makes one חייב whenever the amount fits some animal (six, four or three לוג), and פטור if it is less. רב אשי adds that the רבנן compare the same kind of service, burning with burning, but not pouring with burning. The גמרא then asks whether a loss that happens after an offering leaves the עזרה counts as 'lacking'. Two attempted proofs fail, because each source can be read as a loss that happened inside. Next, three answers explain why one is חייב for אימורים offered outside on top of meat, even though the meat seems to be a חציצה. A new משנה rules that a קומץ mixed back into its מנחה, then offered outside, still makes one חייב, and רבי זירא uses a גזירה שוה to show the שירים do not cancel it. Another משנה discusses offering only the קומץ or only the לבונה outside, and רבי יצחק נפחא's question about what the קומץ alone does to the שירים ends in תיקו. The amud closes with the start of a new משנה about sprinkling part of the blood outside.

steps.title: The argument is about whether putting incense in a vessel matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the root of the argument. רבי אליעזר holds that setting aside קטורת in a vessel makes it one fixed unit. The רבנן hold that the vessel changes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The case is where he set aside the incense] in a vessel. One master holds that setting it aside in a vessel is significant. The other master holds that it is not significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering what רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree about: whether placing קטורת in a vessel makes it a fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, once a larger amount of קטורת is placed in a vessel, the whole amount has to be burned together. So burning only a כזית of it outside is not a complete offering, and he is פטור. For the רבנן, the vessel does not tie the amount together. So a כזית burned outside is still a real offering, and he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting aside an amount by placing it in a vessel
It is something significant; it matters
It is nothing; it does not matter
One master holds (introduces each side of an argument)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a vessel can fix an amount into one unit is the tool רבא uses in the next steps.

phrases.english: in a vessel.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: קְבִיעוּת מָנָא מִילְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: One master holds: setting aside in a vessel is significant,
and one master holds: it is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: קְבִיעוּת מָנָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, started just before this section, to the question of what the two sides argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether placing an amount in a vessel makes it one fixed unit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying point of argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן?

steps.title: Wine set aside for a bull, part offered outside
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows the view that the vessel does not matter. If someone set aside six לוג of wine for a פר, then took four לוג and poured them outside, he is חייב, because four לוג is the right amount for an איל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: According to the one who says setting aside in a vessel is nothing: if one set aside six [לוג] for a bull, took four of them, and offered them outside, he is liable, because they are fit for a ram.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the רבנן's view, that the vessel does not matter, and applies it to wine נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פר needs six לוג of wine, an איל needs four, and a כבש needs three. The vessel does not lock the six לוג together. So the four לוג that were taken out count on their own as a full offering for an איל. That is why pouring them outside makes him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside or designated
He drew out or removed
Outside the עזרה, where offering is forbidden
Fit or suitable
A bull / a ram

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not giving his own opinion about the vessel. He is only working out what follows from the view that the vessel does not matter.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now, according to the one who says
setting aside in a vessel is nothing at all –
if he set aside six for a bull,
phrases.notes: Six לוג of wine, the amount needed for the נסכים of a פר.

phrases.english: and removed four of them
and offered them outside – he is liable;
since they are fit for a ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קְבִיעוּתָא דְּמָנָא וְלָא כְּלוּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the view of the רבנן from step 1 and applies it from קטורת to wine נסכים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the view that the vessel does not matter, offering four לוג outside out of six that were set aside for a פר makes him חייב, because four לוג is a full amount for an איל.

steps.title: Wine set aside for a ram, part offered outside
steps.stepSummary: Using the same logic: if someone set aside four לוג for an איל, then took three and poured them outside, he is חייב, because three לוג is the right amount for a כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set aside four for a ram, took three of them, and offered them outside, he is liable, because they are fit for a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second example that works the same way, one level smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether the smaller amount is a real amount for some animal. Three לוג is exactly what a כבש needs, so offering it outside counts as a real offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb, whose wine offering is three לוג
Three (לוג)

phrases.english: If he set aside four for a ram,
and removed three of them
and offered them outside – he is liable,
since they are fit for a lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָבַע אַרְבָּעָה לְאַיִל, וּמָשַׁךְ מֵהֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case in רבא's same statement, with smaller amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering three לוג outside out of four that were set aside for an איל makes him חייב, because three לוג is a full amount for a כבש.

steps.title: Less than three לוג offered outside: exempt
steps.stepSummary: If the wine is even a little less than three לוג, it is not the right amount for any animal. So pouring it outside makes him פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were lacking any amount at all, and he offered them outside, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his statement by showing where the liability stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוג is the smallest wine offering there is. Anything less is not fit for any animal, so it is not considered a real offering, and there is no liability for pouring it outside.

keyTerms.meaning: They were lacking even the smallest amount
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that the vessel does not matter, offering wine outside makes a person חייב whenever the amount is right for some animal (six, four, or three לוג). Less than three לוג makes him פטור.

phrases.english: If they were lacking any amount at all,
phrases.notes: This means the three לוג from the case just before, if they are even slightly short.

phrases.english: and he offered them outside – he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָסְרוּ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא, וְהִקְרִיבָן בַּחוּץ – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the lower limit for the cases in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine offered outside that is less than three לוג does not make him חייב, because it is not fit for any animal.

steps.title: רב אשי: the רבנן compare the same service, not the same location
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the רבנן do not learn ניסוך from הקטרה, even though both are 'outer.' But they do learn one הקטרה from another הקטרה, even when one is 'outer' and one is 'inner.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The רבנן do not learn the rules of pouring wine from the rules of burning. Even though both are 'outer' services, they don't learn one from the other. But they do learn burning from burning, even though one is 'outer' and the other is 'inner.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי agrees that רבא's wine cases show the רבנן do not learn ניסוך from הקטרה. He then limits that point: for the רבנן, what counts is whether it is the same type of service, not where it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the strongest comparison is between two services done in the same area ('outer' with 'outer'). רב אשי says no. The רבנן care whether it is the same act. So burning can be learned from burning even across 'inner' and 'outer,' but pouring cannot be learned from burning even though both are 'outer.'

keyTerms.meaning: pouring wine (or water) on the מזבח
burning an offering or קטורת
they learn / derive one law from another
here: an 'outer' service, not done in the innermost area
here: an 'inner' service, done in the innermost area

steps.confusionAlert: In this step חוץ and פנים mean 'outer' and 'inner' kinds of service in the מקדש. They do NOT mean 'outside the עזרה,' which is what חוץ meant in the cases of offering outside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for how the רבנן compare services when they work out the amount for being חייב: the same act can be compared, a different act cannot.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Pouring a libation from burning
the Rabbis do not derive.
Even though it is outer from outer,
phrases.notes: Here 'outer' means an outer service in the מקדש, not 'outside the עזרה' like in our earlier cases.

phrases.english: they do not derive it.
But burning from burning they do derive,
even though it is outer from inner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: נִיסּוּךְ מֵהַקְטָרָה לָא יָלְפִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to what follows from רבא's cases in steps 2-4. There the wine amount is set by what fits an animal, not by the כזית used for קטורת. So the רבנן clearly do not learn ניסוך from הקטרה. רב אשי accepts this, but says it does not stop them from learning one הקטרה from another הקטרה, even 'outer' from 'inner.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the rule for comparison: same act, not same location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רבנן won't compare two 'outer' services, you might think they would never compare 'outer' with 'inner.'
steps.terutzMaskana: They do compare when it is the same act (burning with burning), even across 'inner' and 'outer.'

steps.title: Does a loss that happened outside count as lacking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about offerings that were lacking. It asks whether a loss that happened after the item was taken outside the עזרה counts as 'lacking.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And all of them that were lacking' (one who offers them outside is פטור). A question was asked: if the loss happened outside, is it called 'lacking' or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line of the משנה and asking a question about it. This step sets up the question; the next step explains both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says that if the offering is lacking, offering it outside makes one פטור. What is unclear is the case where the item was whole inside, was carried outside, and only then lost some of its amount. Does that later loss still exempt him?

keyTerms.meaning: 'and all of them that were lacking' (the משנה's words)
a question was asked to them (an open question)
a lack / missing amount
it is called / it counts as

phrases.english: "And all of them that were lacking."
A question was raised before them:
A lack that happened outside,
is it considered a lack
or is it not considered a lack?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: חֶסְרוֹן דְּחוּץ, שְׁמֵיהּ חֶסְרוֹן אוֹ לָא שְׁמֵיהּ חֶסְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on a different line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a loss that happens after leaving the עזרה counts as 'lacking' and exempts one who offers it outside.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Side one: once it left, it is already פסול, so being lacking adds nothing. Side two: the Torah makes you חייב only for an item that left whole, not one that is no longer whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: since it went out, it already became פסול, so what difference does it make whether it is lacking or whole? Or perhaps: an item that went out is a reason to be חייב only when it is still whole, but not when it is no longer whole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the question it just asked. It does not answer the question here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: leaving the עזרה already makes the item פסול, and still the Torah makes you חייב for offering it outside. So one more problem, being lacking, should change nothing. Side two: that rule was only said about an item that left in its original, whole state. An item that also lost part of its amount may be too far gone to make one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: they became פסול (unfit)
what difference does it make to me
an offering that left the עזרה
in its original, whole state

phrases.english: Do we say:
since it went out, they became disqualified,
phrases.notes: He means: the Torah still makes you חייב for offering it outside, even though leaving already made it פסול.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חָסֵר מָה לִי יָתֵר;
phrases.english: so what difference is it to me if it is lacking or if it is complete;
or perhaps,
an item that went out and is still in its original state, yes (one is liable),
but one that is not in its original state, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דִּנְפַק – אִיפַּסְלוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning on both sides of the question asked in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חיוב for a יוצא depends on the item still being whole, or whether one problem (leaving) already makes a second problem (lacking) irrelevant.

steps.title: אביי tries to prove the answer from רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the משנה: רבי אליעזר says a person is פטור unless he offers the entire item outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear. רבי אליעזר says he is פטור unless he offers all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to answer the question from step 6. He points to רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says you are only חייב if you offer the whole item outside. That shows the item has to be complete. So if it became lacking at any point, even after it left, it is no longer the whole item, and there would be no חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts; rules the person is not liable
Until he offers
All of them; the entire amount

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Eliezer exempts him
until he offers all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the two sides laid out in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: A loss that happens after the item leaves the עזרה still counts as 'lacking.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: רבי אליעזר פוטר עד שיקריב את כולן.

steps.title: But the question was about the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן objects: how can you prove anything from רבי אליעזר, when the רבנן disagree with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן said to אביי: Do you, Master, settle the question from רבי אליעזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן challenges אביי's proof. Proving something from רבי אליעזר does not answer a question asked according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר. They hold that even a כזית offered outside makes you חייב, so for them the item does not have to be whole. The question in step 6 was asked according to the רבנן, so רבי אליעזר's need for a whole item proves nothing about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Settles or resolves a question
Master; a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
From Rabbi Eliezer the Master resolves it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source אביי used in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question follows the רבנן, and they disagree with רבי אליעזר about needing the whole item.

steps.title: רב: with a lacking item, the רבנן agree
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he heard directly from רב: the רבנן only argue when the item is complete. When it is lacking, they agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it clearly from רב. The רבנן only argue with רבי אליעזר when the item is still whole. But when it is lacking, they agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his proof. He quotes רב, who says that in a case of a lacking item, the רבנן hold the same as רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's view that a כזית is enough applies only when someone offers part of an item that is still whole. If the item itself is already lacking, the רבנן also say פטור. So in a case of lacking, רבי אליעזר's view counts for the רבנן too.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearly, word for word
I heard
They only argue up to this point; the limit of a disagreement
It is still in its original, complete form
Lacking; a missing amount
They agree

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: He said to him: I heard explicitly from Rav:
The Rabbis disagree only
with Rabbi Eliezer
where it is still in its original form;
but where it is lacking, they agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the dispute: the רבנן agree with רבי אליעזר when the item is lacking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר in every case, so he cannot be used for their view.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the item is lacking, the רבנן agree, so רבי אליעזר's view applies to them too.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now the question depends on what kind of 'lacking' רב meant. That is exactly what the next steps examine.

steps.title: Maybe רב means it became lacking outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב's 'lacking' case is one where the loss happened outside the עזרה, which would answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about where it became lacking outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use רב's teaching as the proof. Maybe רב was talking about an item that became lacking after it was taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב's lacking case is a loss that happened outside, then the רבנן agree that such a loss makes the person פטור. That would answer step 6: a loss outside does count as lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it? It introduces a suggested reading
It became lacking
Outside the עזרה

phrases.english: Is it not where it became lacking outside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a proof out of רב's teaching from step 10.
steps.raayaObject: A loss outside the עזרה counts as lacking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that the רבנן agree in a case of חסרון.

steps.title: No, it became lacking inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: רב may mean an item that was already lacking inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about where it became lacking inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 11. רב's case can be read as a loss that happened inside, before the item was taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item was already lacking when it left the עזרה, everyone agrees it is lacking. That says nothing about a loss that happens only after it left, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: No; the גמרא is turning down the proof
Inside the עזרה
The Temple courtyard

phrases.english: No, where it became lacking inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject רב's teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's 'lacking' can mean a loss that happened inside, so it does not touch the question about a loss outside.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a loss outside does NOT count. It only shows that this source does not prove either way.

steps.title: Another proof from the משנה's 'lacking' line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's line that lacking items offered outside are פטור. It suggests the line means a loss that happened outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: all of them that were lacking, and he offered them outside, he is פטור. Isn't that talking about where it became lacking outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof, the very line of the משנה the question was based on. It suggests the משנה means items that became lacking after they left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says lacking items offered outside make you פטור. If the loss there happened outside, this directly answers step 6: such a loss counts as lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: That became lacking
He offered them
Exempt; not liable

phrases.english: Come and hear: And all of them that were lacking
and he offered them outside, he is exempt.
Is it not where it became lacking outside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רב falls in step 12, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: A loss outside the עזרה counts as lacking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: וכולן שחסרו והקריבן בחוץ פטור.

steps.title: Again, it may mean lacking inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way: the משנה may be talking about items that became lacking inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about where it became lacking inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns down the second proof with the same answer it gave in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה can be read as items that were already lacking before they were taken out. So the case of a loss that happened only outside is still not settled.

keyTerms.meaning: That became lacking inside; the reading that blocks both proofs
Rejection of a proof

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason. Each source can be read as an item that became lacking inside the עזרה, so neither one tells us what happens with a loss outside.

phrases.english: No, where it became lacking inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13, just as step 12 rejected step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can mean a loss that happened inside, so it does not cover a loss outside.

steps.title: Why is he liable if the meat blocks the fats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one who offers sacrificial meat with the אימורים outside is חייב. It asks why, since the meat seems to be a חציצה between the אימורים and the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who offers sacrificial items' outside is liable. Why? Isn't there a blocking in between?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and challenging it. If the meat is on the bottom and the אימורים are on top, the meat seems to block the אימורים from the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule behind the question is that someone is only חייב for offering outside if the offering would have been valid inside the עזרה. Inside, a חציצה between the אימורים and the מזבח's fire would make the offering invalid. So the outside offering should not make him חייב either.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? A question asking for the reason behind a ruling
But isn't there...? Used to point out a problem
Something that blocks, an interruption between two things that should touch
The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the meat. Everyone agrees he is פטור for the meat, since meat is not burned on the מזבח. The question is why he is חייב for the אימורים when the meat is underneath them.

phrases.english: One who offers sacrificial items
Why? But there is a blocking!
phrases.notes: The meat underneath is blocking the אימורים on top from touching the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of lacking items (Steps 10-14) to a new line in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who offers meat with אימורים outside is חייב for the אימורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability outside depends on the offering being valid inside. A חציצה would make it invalid inside, so there should be no liability outside.

steps.title: שמואל: He flipped them over
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the pieces were turned over, so the אימורים lay directly on the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it is talking about when he turned them over.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by explaining the case differently. The אימורים were turned over so they touch the fire directly, and the meat is on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל accepts the rule that a חציצה would be a problem. He solves it by changing the picture of the case. With the אימורים on the bottom, nothing blocks them from the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: When he turned them over

phrases.english: Shmuel said: When he turned them over.
phrases.notes: He means the pieces were flipped so the אימורים end up on the bottom, touching the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat was underneath, blocking the אימורים from the fire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אימורים were turned to the bottom, so there is no חציצה at all.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that even without flipping, he is חייב, because the משנה follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that one is חייב even for offering on a rock outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: you can even say he did not turn them over. Whose opinion is this? It is רבי שמעון, who says that even if he offered it on a rock, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer. He keeps the case as it is, with the meat underneath, and says the משנה follows רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that one is חייב for offering on a rock outside, even though a rock is nothing like the מזבח. So for him, the outside offering does not need to match exactly how it would be done inside. Even if the meat would be a חציצה inside, he is still חייב outside.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Introduces an answer that keeps the simpler reading
Whose opinion is this?
A rock

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
You can even say that he did not turn them over;
and whose is this? It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הֶעֱלָה עַל הַסֶּלַע – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: who says: Even if he offered it up on a rock, he is liable.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's opinion from earlier in the פרק, on דף ק״ח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to Step 15, disagreeing with שמואל's need to flip the pieces.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liability outside requires the offering to be valid inside, so a חציצה should make him פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, the outside offering does not need to match the inside method, so he is חייב even with the meat underneath.

steps.title: רב: The same kind does not block
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that there is no חציצה at all, because one kind of substance touching the same kind does not count as blocking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a substance on the same kind of substance does not block.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a third answer. Because the meat and the אימורים come from the same animal, the meat does not count as blocking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יוחנן, רב says the offering would be valid even inside the עזרה. The meat and the אימורים are the same kind, so there is no חציצה in the first place. Since it is valid inside, he is חייב outside, without needing to flip the pieces or rely on רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: A substance together with its own kind
Does not block, does not count as a חציצה

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers for why there is no problem of חציצה: שמואל says the אימורים were flipped onto the fire. רבי יוחנן says רבי שמעון does not require the outside offering to match the inside one. רב says the same kind of substance does not block at all.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A substance with its own kind does not block.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מִין בְּמִינוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to Step 15, different from both שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what counts as a חציצה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat underneath is a חציצה between the אימורים and the fire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The same kind of substance does not block, so the offering is valid even inside, and he is חייב outside.

steps.title: A meal offering offered outside before and after the handful was taken
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that offering a מנחה outside before its קומץ was taken makes one פטור. Once the קומץ was taken, even if it went back into the rest, offering it outside makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a meal offering never had its handful taken, and someone offered it outside, he is exempt. If the handful was taken and then went back into the rest of the offering, and he offered it outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two cases of offering a מנחה outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the קמיצה, the מנחה is not yet ready to be burned on the מזבח inside, so there is no חיוב for offering it outside. After the קמיצה, the קומץ is ready to be burned, so offering it outside makes one חייב. This holds even when it is mixed back in with the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made of flour
The handful of the מנחה that is taken out and burned on the מזבח
Had its handful taken out
Outside the Temple courtyard
Exempt from punishment
Liable to punishment

phrases.english: MISHNA
A meal offering from which a handful was not taken,
and one offered it outside – he is exempt.
If he took its handful, and its handful went back into it,
and he offered it outside – he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The previous sugya about חציצה on the fire has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unready מנחה (no קמיצה) offered outside makes one פטור. A קומץ that was taken and mixed back in, offered outside, makes one חייב.

steps.title: Why don't the leftovers cancel out the handful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one is חייב in the second case. The שירים are much bigger than the קומץ, so they should cancel it out through ביטול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why is he liable? Let the leftovers cancel out the handful!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second ruling of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a small amount mixed into a large amount of something else loses its identity, which is called ביטול. If the קומץ were cancelled inside the שירים, the mixture would just count as שירים, which are not burned on the מזבח. Then offering it outside should not make one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
The leftover part of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken, eaten by the כהנים
Let them cancel out (ביטול, a small amount losing its identity in a larger amount)

phrases.english: GEMARA
But why?
Let the leftovers cancel out the handful!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, some the word in square brackets. Both mean 'cancel out.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חייב ruling in the second case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one is חייב for offering outside a קומץ that was mixed back into the שירים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The larger שירים should cancel out the smaller קומץ, so the mixture should count as plain שירים, which carry no חיוב.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the leftovers do not cancel the handful
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'burning,' which is said about both the קומץ and the שירים. Just as one קומץ cannot cancel another, the שירים cannot cancel a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The word 'burning' is used for the handful, and the word 'burning' is used for the leftovers. Just as one handful does not cancel another handful, so too the leftovers do not cancel the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question: the שירים don't cancel the קומץ, so the mixture still holds a real קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the word הקטרה for both the קומץ and the שירים. That shared word links them. Two קמצים mixed together don't cancel each other, so the שירים, which are linked to the קומץ by that word, don't cancel a קומץ either. Because the קומץ stays important, offering the mixture outside makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning on the מזבח
Learning one law from another because the תורה uses the same word in both places
'Just as ... so too', the formula for comparing two cases
Cancels out

steps.whatToRemember: The שירים do not cancel out a קומץ mixed into them, because a גזירה שוה from 'burning' compares them to two קמצים, which never cancel each other. So the קומץ stays a קומץ, and offering it outside makes one חייב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
'Burning' is said about the handful,
and 'burning' is said about the leftovers;
just as with the burning of the handful –
one handful does not cancel another,
so too with the burning of the leftovers –
the leftovers do not cancel the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: נֶאֶמְרָה הַקְטָרָה בַּקּוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a source (a גזירה שוה) showing that the normal rule of ביטול does not apply here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The large amount of שירים should cancel the small קומץ, like any normal mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the גזירה שוה from הקטרה, the שירים cannot cancel the קומץ, so the משנה's חייב ruling stands.

steps.title: Offering only the handful or only the frankincense outside
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if someone offers only the קומץ or only the לבונה outside, the תנא קמא says he is חייב. רבי אליעזר says he is פטור until he offers the second one too. If one was offered inside and one outside, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The handful and the frankincense: if someone offered one of them outside, he is liable. רבי אליעזר exempts him until he offers the second one. If one was offered inside and one outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks what happens when only one of the two burned parts of a מנחה is offered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ and the לבונה are both burned for a מנחה. The תנא קמא treats each one as its own offering, so offering just one outside makes one חייב. רבי אליעזר sees them as one unit, so offering just one outside does not make one חייב. In the final case, one inside and one outside, the ruling is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, burned on the מזבח together with the קומץ of a מנחה
Exempts
Inside the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רבי אליעזר exempts only when one part is offered outside and the other part is not offered at all. When one is offered inside and the other outside, the ruling is חייב.

phrases.english: MISHNA
The handful and the frankincense,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: if one offered one of them outside – he is liable.
Rabbi Eliezer exempts him
until he offers the second.
One inside and one outside – he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹמֶץ וְהַלְּבוֹנָה שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a related topic, the two burned parts of a מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: offering either the קומץ or the לבונה alone outside makes one חייב. רבי אליעזר: פטור until both are offered outside. One inside and one outside: חייב.

steps.title: The two bowls of frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a parallel case. Offering one of the two bowls of לבונה outside makes one חייב. רבי אליעזר says he is פטור until he offers the second. If one was offered inside and one outside, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two bowls of frankincense: if he offered one of them outside, he is liable. רבי אליעזר exempts him until he offers the second. If one was offered inside and one outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case that works just like the קומץ and לבונה case. This time it is the two bowls of לבונה that are burned to permit the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two bowls together permit the bread, just as the קומץ and לבונה together permit the שירים. The תנא קמא says each one alone counts as a real offering, so offering one outside makes him חייב. רבי אליעזר holds that only both together count, but he agrees that when one was offered inside and the other outside, he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl. Two bowls of לבונה were placed with the לחם הפנים.
Frankincense
The showbread on the שולחן. It may be eaten only after the לבונה is burned.
Exempts from punishment

phrases.english: Two bowls of frankincense,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: where he offered one of them outside, he is liable.
Rabbi Eliezer exempts him,
until he offers the second one.
One inside and one outside: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה, שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to the קומץ and לבונה ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering one of two permitting items outside makes one חייב according to the תנא קמא. רבי אליעזר says one is פטור until both are offered. If one was offered inside and one outside, he is חייב.

steps.title: Does the קומץ alone permit half the remainder?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא asks about burning only the קומץ without the לבונה. Does that fully permit its matching half of the שירים, or does it only weaken the prohibition?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יצחק נפחא asked: the קומץ, does it permit the matching part of the remainder? Does it truly permit it, or does it only weaken the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question from רבי יצחק נפחא. Once the קומץ is burned but not yet the לבונה, what has happened to the שירים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ and the לבונה together permit all of the שירים, so maybe each one 'covers' half. The question has two possible answers. Either the קומץ fully permits its half right away, or it only makes the איסור weaker while all the שירים stay forbidden until the לבונה is burned too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that has no ready answer (a dilemma)
Does it really permit, completely
Does it only weaken the prohibition
Its matching share

steps.confusionAlert: Even the second option ('weakening') does not mean any of the שירים may be eaten yet. It means the איסור on them is no longer at full strength.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha asked:
The handful: what is the law, does it permit
its matching part of the remainder?
phrases.notes: He means the half of the שירים that the קומץ is responsible for. The לבונה would take care of the other half.

phrases.english: Does it truly permit it,
or does it only weaken the prohibition?
phrases.notes: Some versions read קלושי, in round brackets. The corrected wording is אקלושי, in square brackets. Both mean 'weaken.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's idea that the קומץ and לבונה together permit the שירים, and asks what one of them does alone.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether burning the קומץ alone fully permits half of the שירים, or only weakens the prohibition on them.

steps.title: According to whom is this question asked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question itself. According to רבי מאיר, the קומץ obviously permits its half. According to the רבנן, it obviously does nothing at all. Either way, there seems to be nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this question? If according to רבי מאיר, who says one can make פיגול with half of what permits, then it surely permits! If according to the רבנן, who say one cannot make פיגול with half of what permits, then it neither permits nor weakens!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק נפחא's question. It shows that under both well-known opinions about פיגול, the answer is already clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a wrong intention during just one of the two permitting acts makes the offering פיגול. That shows each act has real power alone, so the קומץ should fully permit its half. The רבנן require the wrong intention during both acts, which shows one act alone does nothing, so the קומץ should not even weaken the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?
One can make an offering פיגול through a wrong intention
Half of what permits: one of the two acts that together permit the offering
An offering ruined by an intention to eat or burn it at the wrong time

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the sugya. The גמרא will now have to find a way to explain רבי יצחק נפחא's question so that it is still a real question.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If according to Rabbi Meir,
who says: one can make it piggul with half of what permits,
then it surely truly permits!
If according to the Rabbis, who say:
one cannot make it piggul with half of what permits,
then it neither truly permits,
nor does it weaken!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Some versions have the word in round brackets instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question of step 24 by showing it seems to have an obvious answer under each opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's question about whether the קומץ alone permits or weakens.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מחלוקת about פיגול with half of what permits already decides how much power one permitting act has alone. Under רבי מאיר it fully permits, and under the רבנן it does nothing, so no opinion leaves room for the question.

steps.title: Maybe the question follows רבי אליעזר? No.
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question was asked according to רבי אליעזר, then rejects this. רבי אליעזר agrees with the רבנן that half a מתיר cannot create פיגול, so for him there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe the question was asked according to רבי אליעזר? No. רבי אליעזר holds like the רבנן, who say you cannot make an offering פיגול with only half of the things that permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: Step 25 said there is nothing to ask, either according to רבי מאיר or according to the רבנן. Now the גמרא tries a third option, רבי אליעזר, and quickly rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says one is פטור for offering only the קומץ outside, so for him one half alone is not a real offering. That matches the רבנן who say half a מתיר does nothing for פיגול. So according to רבי אליעזר, the קומץ alone neither permits nor weakens anything, and again there is no question.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: Rather, was it asked according to Rabbi Eliezer?
Rabbi Eliezer holds like the Rabbis,
who say: one cannot make an offering piggul with half of what permits it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a new setting for the question after step 25 ruled out רבי מאיר and the רבנן, then rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects placing רבי יצחק נפחא's question according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר agrees that half a מתיר has no power at all, so the question would have an obvious answer.

steps.title: The question follows the רבנן of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the question follows the רבנן of this משנה, who make one חייב for just the קומץ outside. So for them each half has some power. The question is whether that power fully permits half the שירים or only weakens the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was asked according to the רבנן here, in our משנה. What is the law? Does burning the קומץ fully permit its half of the שירים, or does it only weaken the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 25 by finding the right opinion for the question, and then restates the question itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are a different group of רבנן from the ones about פיגול. The תנא קמא of our משנה says offering only the קומץ outside makes one חייב, which shows one half alone counts for something. Since it clearly does something, the question becomes real: does it fully permit half, or only weaken the prohibition on the whole?

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis of this משנה here, the תנא קמא of step 22
Fully permits
Only weakens, making the prohibition less strong without removing it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups called רבנן. The רבנן of step 25 argue with רבי מאיר about פיגול. The רבנן of step 27 are the תנא קמא of our משנה, who argue with רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the question only makes sense for someone who holds that half a מתיר has some power, but not obviously full power.

phrases.english: Rather, it was asked according to the Rabbis here.
phrases.notes: "Here" means our משנה from step 22, where the first opinion says he is חייב for the קומץ alone.

phrases.english: What is the law? Does it fully permit,
or does it only weaken the prohibition?
phrases.notes: Some versions say קָלֵישׁ, in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is אִקְּלוֹשֵׁי. The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי אליעזר in step 26, identifies the correct opinion for the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the specific opinion under which the question is valid.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under every known view, the answer seemed obvious, so the question seemed pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא of our משנה, each half has some power, so it is a real question whether that power is full permission or only weakening.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. It is not settled whether the קומץ alone fully permits half or only weakens the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי יצחק נפחא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source was found to decide between full permission and mere weakening. The question stays open, and the discussion ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן of our משנה, burning only the קומץ does something. Whether it fully permits half the שירים or only weakens the prohibition stays unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.title: New משנה: sprinkling part of the blood outside
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins with someone who sprinkles only part of an offering's blood outside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sprinkles part of the blood outside the עזרה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה. This line only sets up the case, and the ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was offering part of a מנחה outside. Now the same kind of question moves to blood: what if only some of the blood is sprinkled outside, like one sprinkling instead of all of them?

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, marking the start of a new משנה
One who sprinkles or throws the blood on the מזבח
Part of the blood
Outside the עזרה, the Temple courtyard
